title: Guidance Note on Cluster Simplification and Adapting In-Country Coordination
summary: The reference point for the current reshaping of coordination. Reduces the system to eight clusters — nutrition, protection, shelter/land/site coordination, WASH, education, food security, health, and logistics with telecommunications — and carries an annex on lead and accountability arrangements for consolidated clusters. WASH remains standalone. The adapting-to-context half is where area-based arrangements are addressed at inter-agency level.

title: Reference Module for Cluster Coordination at Country Level
summary: The foundational description of what a cluster is for and what its core functions are. Everything in the transition and area-based material assumes it. This is the July 2015 revision — an older 2012 edition also circulates, so check the date on any copy you are handed.

title: Q&A: the process of cluster simplification within the Humanitarian Reset
summary: Plainer answers to the questions country teams were actually asking about simplification, written before the March 2026 guidance settled them.

title: Understanding and influencing the IASC system at country level
summary: Written for NGOs rather than for cluster staff. Useful if the question is how a partner gets a decision changed rather than how the structure is meant to work.

title: Guidance on Cluster Transition and Deactivation
summary: The normative basis for deactivation: when the conditions for activation are no longer met, and what a phased handover is expected to involve. Sets out that transition is a change in how coordination is arranged, not an end to it.

title: Checklist for HCs and HCTs on Cluster Transition and Deactivation
summary: The operational companion to the guidance — what a humanitarian coordinator and country team are expected to have done before a deactivation decision.

title: Annex B — example template for a transition strategy
summary: A worked template rather than a narrative document. The starting structure if a country is drafting a transition strategy from nothing.

title: Summary of the Guidance on Cluster Transition and Deactivation
summary: The short version of the full guidance. The one to circulate to an HCT or a partner meeting when nobody will read forty pages.

title: Protection Field Coordination Toolkit — Chapter 8: Cluster Transition and Deactivation
summary: Another sector's version of the same problem, and the clearest single statement of the rule that matters most here: lack of funding, political challenges, security or lead-agency capacity are not reasons to deactivate a cluster if coordination is still needed and national structures cannot provide it. Also carries a short area-based coordination section.

title: Standard Terms of Reference for Area-Based Coordination
summary: Newly issued. The first standard terms of reference for area-based coordination at inter-agency level — which matters because the absence of one is a documented problem in this evidence base, not a theoretical gap.

title: Guidance Note for Coordination in Urban Crises
summary: The pre-2026 inter-agency reference for area-based working, written for urban response. Still the document other guidance points to for practical tips, which is itself a sign of how thin the ABC guidance shelf has been.

title: Area-Based Development Practice Note
summary: The development-side framing of area-based working. Useful where the successor arrangement is a development platform rather than a humanitarian one, which is a live question in several transition contexts.
